sentences.text:
Assailing the award dated 7/9/2015 passed by Member, 10th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
District Gwalior in Claim Case No. 210/2013, on the point of inadequacy of the compensation, the appellant has preferred this appeal for enhancement of award under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

entities.text:
10th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
District Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The accident in question took place on 26/2/13 in which the appellant sustained grievous injuries in both her legs including fractures.

2. Appellant/claimant had filed the claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.21,00,000/- for the bodily injuries suffered by appellant/claimant in the accident which took place on 26/2/2013.
However, Claims Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,13,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of application.

3. Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 26/2/13 when appellant alongwith her daugther were going on his Scooty, it is alleged that due to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:13705 2 MA-1189-2015 rash and negligent driving of auto driver of Auto No. MP32R0757, Auto dashed the scooty, due to which both fell down from the scooty and sustained grievous injuries, therefore, she moved a claim petition.

sentences.text: Shri Gupta, learned counsel representing the appellant, contends that the injuries sustained by the appellant were grievous in nature.
She suffered multiple fractures in both leg and also suffered fracture in ribs.
After the accident she could not work for long period.
After the accident she is not being able to do the work which she used to prior to the accident for her livelihood i.e. dairy work.
The Tribunal erred in disbelieving the disability caused to appellant.

The Tribunal has only awarded Rs. 3,13,400/- towards loss of income, medical expenses, Special diet and pain and suffering and transportation ectc. which is on the lower side, thus the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is inadequate, without looking to the nature of grievous injuries sustained, hospitalization and medical bills.
In view of the foregoing submissions, the enhancement of the compensation so awarded by the Tribunal, has been prayed for.
5. On the other hand, Shri Malhotra, learned counsel representing the respondent/Insurance Company, supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

6. After having heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and on perusal of the pleadings and the evidence so adduced, in the opinion of this Court, considering the nature of injuries, treatment papers and its period, the mental pain and suffering and also the other heads, the compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal is liable to be enhanced by Rs. 8,000/- in lump sum thereby making the total compensation 3,21,400/-which shall be NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:13705 3 MA-1189-2015 paid within two months from today.
7. In view of the forgoing discussions, the appeal succeeds and is hereby allowed in part.
The appellant is held entitled to receive the enhanced amount of Rs. 8,000/- in addition to the amount of compensation already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as per impugned award from the date of filing claim case.
The other conditions including liability of payment of compensation amount as imposed by claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
8. With the aforesaid modification in the impugned award, the appeal stands allowed in part.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
JAI PRAKASH SOLANKI 2024.08.20 14:39:56 +05'30'
